limitations: Phase 4 did not record training-set metrics, so a train-versus-test gap cannot be reported and no conclusion about overfitting can be drawn from this run.
All models use baseline (untuned) parameters; the ranking describes the default configuration of each algorithm, not the best configuration it could reach.
The hold-out result comes from a single train/test split (one random_state), so it is one estimate of generalisation, not a repeated-measures estimate.
Per-class precision, recall and F1 are derived from the confusion matrix of the hold-out split only; they are not validated against a second measurement.
Execution times come from one run on one machine without repetitions, so they are indicative only and must not be read as a benchmark.

final_model.selection_reason: The best valid baseline model is persisted because no usable optimized model was available. The Phase 5 evaluation result is preserved unchanged. Optimization status: not_started. Selected: baseline Logistic Regression (hold-out f1_score 0.8761).
final_model.selection_rule: Final model selection reuses the project's existing ranking: primary f1_score (descending), secondary accuracy (descending), then the model name (ascending) as the final tie-break. The optimized candidate is the Phase 6 winner (best_optimized_model) and the baseline candidate is the Phase 4/5 winner (best_baseline_model); both are compared on the hold-out split they were already scored on. When optimization was disabled, skipped or produced no usable winner, the baseline candidate is the final model. No new metric and no new threshold is introduced here.
